heuristics: H1: the canonical 32-adding walk on the (r-1)/6 automorphism classes has first-collision time approximating the birthday tail 1 - exp(-t^2/(2N)); supported by classical rho analysis, Teske's r-adding-walk experiments, and the toy run (0.545 vs 0.4845 ideal in the lag-free regime). The 1.15*sqrt(N) budget with the charged cycle-waste factors needs only 87% of the modeled collision probability to clear 0.39.

The fruitless 2-cycle of the negation map has constant-order trigger rate (~1/192 per step, bounded by 1/64); it is detected by a 2-step look-back on the full walk state, escaped with one charged addition, and its waste is charged. Longer fruitless cycles are excluded deterministically (2-term constant relations, setup check), by union bounds (3-8 term relations < 2^-172), and empirically (toy escape counts; Bos-Kleinjung-Lenstra; Galbraith-Hopkins-Shparlinski), with a charged 5% residual efficiency slack.

Instruction sub-costs are analytical worst-case bounds; mod-r arithmetic prices are supplied by explicit constructions (32-instruction addition, 384-instruction multiplication, 2*384+512-instruction inversion), not by transplanting the mod-p measurement.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack with success probability lower bound 0.39 exactly at the protected threshold; no amplification is used and all failures are charged.
The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^63-slot allocation of about 2^70 bytes; overflow aborts with probability < 2^-62 (Chernoff).
Automorphism-accelerated rho is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel attack; this is the first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
